summary: Ward Peak lookout on the Idaho-Montana line: a 1914 cabin, a 1929 L-2 cabin, destroyed in the 1950s; hike-in summit with only a USGS marker and cabin remnants.

facts.design: 1929 L-2 shake cupola cabin, which replaced a cabin dated 1914
facts.status_note: Destroyed in the 1950s; the sources describe only remnants of the cabin on the summit

staffing.status: one known staffer, Herb Uttley, per Idaho Fire Lookouts (citing Bert Russell); no other staffing in the sources read

access.note: Hike-in summit on national forest land; trail #250 from the state-line road. The sources read describe no closure, but do not state public access in terms.

visit.trail_note: Trail #250 from the state-line road (#391), 1.3 miles total to the summit, per Great Burn Lakes; the Little Joe Road (#282) out of St. Regis is the approach

events.note: Cabin constructed on the summit (firelookout.com); Great Burn Lakes says an original cabin was built in 1914
Herb Uttley listed under Known Staff for 1925 (Idaho Fire Lookouts, citing Bert Russell's book); the sources do not say which cabin he used
L-2 shake cupola cabin built (firelookout.com); Great Burn Lakes says it replaced the 1914 cabin
Decade only: all three sources say 'the 1950s' and none gives a year. The brief's 1950 is not supported

evidence.supports: Ward Peak sits on the Idaho/Montana border; a cabin was constructed in 1914
evidence.quote: Located on the Idaho/Montana border, a cabin was constructed here in 1914.

evidence.supports: 1929 cabin was a shake cupola cabin

evidence.supports: the summit today has a USGS survey marker and remnants of the lookout cabin
evidence.quote: The summit has a USGS Survey marker and the remnants of the long-gone lookout cabin.

evidence.quote: The trail then switchbacks up the ridge to the summit of Ward Peak; a total of 1.3 miles.

evidence.quote: Take the Ward Peak trail (#250) straight up the hill from the road.

corrections.why: firelookout.com, Idaho Fire Lookouts and Great Burn Lakes all say the cabin was destroyed in the 1950s; none gives 1950

sources.title: Ward Peak
sources.publisher: Lakes of the Great Burn & More

notes_for_editor: Dates agree across three sources except the brief's '1950', which all three replace with 'the 1950s'. Elevation 7,312 ft from firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts. 'Public' access is inferred from the hike-in description on national forest land; no source states it. Great Burn Lakes is a hiking site, so the summit-remnant claim rests on one source.
